topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class to the final course session and outlines the key learning goals regarding cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Traditional cancer treatment modalities and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss conventional cancer treatment approaches, including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents alongside their mechanisms, toxicities, and resistance.

topics.label: Targeting cancer cell vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer cell defects, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and homologous recombination repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction, kinase inhibitors, and mechanisms of targeted resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogenic driver kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and the molecular mechanisms and management of acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe using engineered antibodies to block oncogenic receptors, recruit immune effector functions, and deliver cytotoxic payloads directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Tumor immune surveillance and cellular immunotherapy strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the role of the immune system in cancer surveillance and methods for unleashing antitumor immune responses using checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, clinical progress, and future directions in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate systemic challenges in cancer treatment, historical survival trends, emerging clinical paradigms, and the ethical considerations of developing novel therapies.
